items.title: Four questions to help you stop overthinking
items.content_snippet: Overthinking feels productive, and that is exactly the trap the research pins down. Sonja Lyubomirsky and Susan Nolen-Hoeksema had people either dwell on themselves or focus on something unrelated, then asked them to solve real problems from their own lives. items.content_snippet: Explore plugin extensions through Meetings and OpenAI Developers. See how a custom interface can live beside a conversation and bring selected context into your work with ChatGPT.

items.title: Stop Overpaying for Intelligence | DevDay 2026
items.content_snippet: Cut AI costs while preserving quality. Learn to measure cost per completed task, choose models and reasoning effort, and use prompt caching, Programmatic Tool Calling, and the Batch API.

items.title: Stack Overflow - From Idea to Product | DevDay 2026
items.content_snippet: See how small teams at Stack Overflow used Codex to build Stack Overflow for Agents and reimagine Stack Internal. Take away lessons for accelerating R&D and bringing new products to market.

items.title: Higgsfield - Building Agents That Provision Their Own Compute | DevDay 2026
items.content_snippet: Explore how Higgsfield agents choose models and provision their own compute. Learn when to use dedicated GPUs or hosted models, how to deliver predictable throughput, and where the approach can fail.

items.title: How OpenAI Puts ChatGPT to Work | DevDay 2026
items.content_snippet: See how OpenAI’s teams use ChatGPT to manage launches, research competitors, and turn expertise into tools. Take practical ideas back to your own work.

items.title: Codex Has Left The Laptop | DevDay 2026
items.content_snippet: Explore what’s new in Codex across the CLI, app, and web. Through live demos, see how to move from delegating individual tasks to letting Codex tackle entire problems and goals.

items.title: From Single Player to Multiplayer with Codex | DevDay 2026
items.content_snippet: Follow a 2am outage from the first Slack message to a reviewed fix. See how voice, Appshots, plugins, and meeting notes help a persistent personal agent investigate and keep the team informed.

items.title: Qodo - The Last Human Code Review | DevDay 2026
items.content_snippet: See how Qodo uses OpenAI to review AI-generated code. Explore an adversarial reviewer that challenges coding agents’ assumptions and output, and learn when model confidence still needs human judgment.

items.title: ClawLabs: Building Open Source Together | DevDay 2026
items.content_snippet: See how agents help small open-source teams build together. Explore workflows for sharing context across projects and working with contributors, with live demos of cloud sessions and computer use.

items.title: Let Anyone at Your Company Ship Internal Apps with AI — Garrett Galow, WorkOS
items.content_snippet: Building an app with AI got cheap. Getting it in front of your coworkers didn't. Garrett Galow from the WorkOS product team shows how WorkOS lets anyone at the company build and ship internal apps. It started when an account executive built a helpful sales chatbot before her leave, and the CEO couldn't even open it. items.title: Giving AI Agents Memory That Learns — Jake Broekhuizen, LangChain
items.content_snippet: Most teams are great at watching what their agents did. Far fewer turn that into lessons for the next run. Jake Broekhuizen from LangChain's Labs team explains how to give agents memory that actually changes their behavior. Using a real financial services agent whose tone kept slipping from advisory to pushy, he shows why traces and logs are only evidence: they become memory only when a lesson turns into durable context the agent reads next time. He breaks memory into semantic, episodic and proc

items.title: Why Bigger Context Windows Won't Save Your Agent — Elizabeth Fuentes Leone, AWS
items.content_snippet: A bigger context window won't save your agent. Past a point, it forgets the middle. Elizabeth Fuentes Leone, developer advocate at AWS, explains why agents break when tools return huge amounts of data, and why bigger context windows aren't the fix: models remember the start and end of a long context but lose the middle. Using the open-source, model-agnostic Strands Agents framework, she walks through four strategies (externalize, select, compress, isolate) with code. She covers sliding-window an

items.title: AI Hackers Are Faster Than Your Pen Test — Eli Cohen, Snyk
items.content_snippet: Attackers use AI too, and the fastest AI attack he cites took four minutes. A pen test once or twice a year can't keep up. Eli Cohen of Snyk, co-founder of the runtime security company Helios, explains why security has to go on the offense in an agent-first world. Developers now ship far more code, much of it insecure, while attackers use frontier models to chain small vulnerabilities into critical ones in minutes. He walks through why traditional tools fall short: static scanning misses runtime

items.title: The Software Factory: From Bug Report to Production Code — Davis Palmie, Factory
items.content_snippet: Engineers are going from typing code to governing agents. The next step is a system that turns bug reports into production code. Davis Palmie, member of technical staff at Factory, explains the software factory: a system of agents that takes input signals like bug reports and user feedback and turns them into production code. items.title: Why Your AI Agents Can't Talk to Each Other (Yet) — Vlad Luzin, BAND
items.content_snippet: If you run Claude and Codex side by side, you're the router passing messages between them. It doesn't have to be that way. Vlad Luzin, co-founder and CTO of BAND, argues the future belongs to AI agents talking to other AI agents, inside companies, between companies, and between businesses and consumers. items.title: Why AI Agents Should Have Their Own Sandbox — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind
items.content_snippet: Your agent shouldn't run on your laptop. Give it its own computer in the cloud, with one API call. Philipp Schmid from Google DeepMind walks through the Gemini Interactions API, Google's new API for both models and agents. It handles server-side state, long-running background jobs, and built-in plus custom tools across text, audio and images, and it replaces user/model turns with a timeline of steps. items.title: Redesigning How Software Gets Built With AI Agents — Sonar & McKinsey Panel
items.content_snippet: Most companies say they've deployed AI agents. Fewer than a third say it's paying off. What do the rest do differently? A panel with Sonar CEO Tariq Shaukat and Ali-Reza Adl-Tabatabai, former CEO of Gitar (now part of Sonar) and former head of Uber's developer platform, moderated by McKinsey. Research with Sonar found the teams getting real results from agents change three things: their process, their tooling and, most often overlooked, their people and roles. items.title: From 36% to 100%: How Self-Improving Agents Write Their Own Skills — Rafal Wilinski, Runlayer
items.content_snippet: When one agent finally cracks a hard problem, what if every agent in the company learned it too? Rafal Wilinski, founding engineer at Runlayer, shows how to go from one self-improving agent to a self-improving company. He explains why skills matter more as agents work longer (a bad start can send them down an hours-long rabbit hole) and the three problems holding skills back: they're built for developers, nobody has time to write them, and many clients don't support them. items.title: Grep or Embeddings? Agentic Search Over Company Documents — George He, LlamaIndex
items.content_snippet: Grep works great on a codebase. Try it on millions of PDFs, slides and scanned schematics. George He, head of engineering at LlamaIndex, explains when agents need pre-indexed search and when plain file traversal is enough. Claude Code skipped embeddings because code is small, text-based, local and full of breadcrumbs. Company data is huge, messy, multimodal and permissioned.
